chunks: And in the narration of Ibrahim ibn Abi Al-Bilad, he said:

There was a woman during the time of Dawud (peace be upon him) to whom a man would come, forcing himself upon her. So Allah, the Exalted and Almighty, inspired her heart, and she said to him: 'You do not come to me once except that there is someone with your family.'

So the man went to his family and found a man with his family. He brought that man to Dawud (peace be upon him) and said: 'O Prophet of Allah, something has happened to me that has not happened to anyone else.'
He said: 'And what is that?' He replied: 'I found this man with my family.'
So Allah, the Exalted, revealed to Dawud (peace be upon him): 'Tell him'
As you deal, so shall you be dealt with.

key_terms.دَاوُدُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Prophet Dawud (David), peace be upon him
key_terms.كَمَا تَدِينُ تُدَانُ: As you deal, so shall you be dealt with (Quranic phrase)
key_terms.يَسْتَكْرِهُهَا: He forces her (referring to sexual coercion)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning and origin of the Quranic phrase 'As you deal, so shall you be dealt with' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narrative from Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih highlights the principle of 'Kama tadinu tudan' (As you deal, so shall you be dealt with) through a specific incident during the time of Prophet Dawud (as). A woman, coerced by a man, was divinely inspired to claim his household had a guest; when he verified this, he brought the man to Dawud, who then received divine revelation establishing this reciprocal justice as a legal and ethical precedent. This event underscores the Shia scholarly understanding of divine inspiration (wahy) extending to prophets for both legislation and specific judicial rulings.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4986 - In the narration of Ibrahim ibn Abi Al-Bilad, it is reported:

"There was a woman during the time of Prophet Dawud (as) (David), whom a man would force himself upon.
Allah (swt), the Almighty and Exalted, inspired her heart, and she said to him: 'You do not come to me except that someone is with your family.'

So the man went to his family and found a man with his wife.
He brought that man to Prophet Dawud (as), and said: 'O' Prophet of Allah (swt), something has happened to me that has never happened to anyone else.'
Dawud (as) asked: 'And what is that?' The man replied: 'I found this man with my wife.'
Then Allah (swt), revealed to Dawud (as), saying: 'Tell him:
As you deal, so shall you be dealt with.'"
